items.title: Live: Iran seizes two ships in the strait, calls on US to lift the blockade
items.description: Iran has said it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the US naval blockade remains in place. Follow live.

items.title: Warning $7,000 NDIS cuts to plans will 'isolate' people with disability
items.description: An average cut of $7,000 to NDIS participant plans could hurt social supports providing the "only interaction with the outside world" for some people with disability, advocates warn, as the minister Mark Butler concedes the savings will have a material impact on participants.

items.title: We haven't seen budget decisions like this since Joe Hockey in 2014
items.description: As far as tough budget decisions go, we haven't seen anything on this scale since Joe Hockey's ill-fated 2014 effort.

items.title: New AI threat looms but Australian firms don't have access needed to prepare
items.description: Local banks, power providers and infrastructure firms do not have access to test their systems against a powerful new AI cybersecurity risk, Anthropic's Mythos, which has not been made public.

items.title: Five per cent home deposit scheme fuelling price hike, report suggests
items.description: New research from property analytics firm Cotality appears to show that the Home Guarantee Scheme, intended to help first home buyers, may be worsening entry level affordability.

items.title: Disability community 'scared' as government defends NDIS overhaul
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler has defended the government's latest cost-cutting changes to the scheme in an interview with the ABC, amid an avalanche of participant concern.

items.title: Pacific leaders 'totally blindsided' by declaration of fuel emergency
items.description: Confusion and some frustration remains after a key Pacific leader announced an emergency declaration had been agreed to over fuel, despite other leaders not knowing about it.

items.title: Australian billionaire's waste-to-energy plan labelled 'waste colonialism'
items.description: The controversial project would see waste burned to create energy in Fiji to reduce the country's reliance on fossil fuels, but locals and environmentalists are not happy.

items.title: Laura says her cop ex was given a 'golden pass' on rape allegations
items.description: When Tasmania Police misidentified Laura as a family violence perpetrator, she had no idea she'd have to fight for them to hold her abuser — a serving officer — to account. Now, she's fighting for change.

items.title: 'Ghosted': Musicians claim gig booker owes thousands of dollars
items.description: A triple j hack investigation uncovers allegations that a booking agency has failed to pay more than 20 Australian bands and artists.

items.title: 70yo 'duped' into importing heroin to Sydney in fold-out camping bed jailed
items.description: Barry James Calverley's lawyers argued he was an innocent drug mule who naively and gullibly trusted a story about why he needed to bring the bed to Australia.

items.title: More than a third of Australians are seeking food relief for the first time
items.description: About one in three people are accessing food relief services for the first time, according to a new report from Food charity OzHarvest.

items.title: EU backs $148bn loan for Ukraine after pipeline spat resolved
items.description: A bitter feud over an oil pipeline pitted Hungary against Ukraine and stalled the vitally needed funds for Kyiv.

items.title: ICC judges reject bid to release former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte
items.description: Earlier hearings heard Rodrigo Duterte was allegedly responsible for thousands of deaths during his war on drugs.

items.title: 'Overpowered' electric motorbikes could still be sold under proposed e-bike laws
items.description: Cycling advocates say as long as the electric dirt bikes are sold for use on private land, they won't have to meet the stringent requirements of regular e-bikes.

items.title: Rescue package 'better than nothing', but uncertainty remains for smelter workers
items.description: Three weeks of wages have been guaranteed for Liberty Bell Bay smelter workers, but with no buyer locked in, questions remain about what happens next.

items.title: 50 years of Ramones — the album nobody bought but everyone copied
items.description: Fed up with where rock'n'roll was headed, these four New Yorkers changed the music world by playing sweet pop hooks at breakneck speed.

items.title: Embattled salmon industry launches advertising blitz amid calls to shut down
items.description: A new advertising campaign featuring the stories of workers adjacent to Tasmania's fish farming industry is launched amid calls for the sector to be shut down.

items.title: New CFA and forest firefighting funding announced
items.description: The state government has unveiled its latest investment in CFA and forest firefighting upgrades.

items.title: Passengers return to Perth Airport after police investigate unattended bag
items.description: Passengers are allowed back into Terminal 1 after an exclusion zone was established at the airport for roughly two hours.

items.title: Police 'not fully prepared' for violent scene they were called to, NT inquest hears
items.description: An inquest hears evidence from a senior police officer who ran into a room to disarm a mother who was self-harming inside a Darwin crisis accommodation facility, describing the incident as "one of the worst days" of her policing career.

items.title: 'Lost everything': New Zealand's capital cleans up as rain pushes north
items.description: Police have found the body of a man as floodwaters recede in New Zealand's capital and the clean-up begins.

items.title: 101yo Bombing of Darwin veteran wants Australians to know what unfolded
items.description: At 101 years old, Bombing of Darwin survivor Terrance Byrne wants Australians to know exactly what unfolded during the World War II attack on Darwin — still the single largest foreign attack on Australian soil.

items.title: Australia ready for AUKUS subs as China threat looms, US commander says
items.description: The US's Indo-Pacific commander praises work to upgrade Australia's AUKUS base, but says he needs more naval firepower in the region as China rapidly expands its military.

items.title: Gaza conditions 'catastrophic' as report finds $US71b needed to rebuild
items.description: More than $US71 billion will be needed over the next 10 years for recovery and reconstruction in Gaza, according to a new report by the European Union and the United Nations.
